title: Utility Order for Delta North Louisiana Gas Company, LLC, Delta South Louisiana Gas Company, LLC and Delta Capital Gas Company, LLC. — Order No. S-37932 accepts the Staff Report and Recommendation filed into the record on July 23, 2026, subject to the changes recommended within, and the Commission expresses its non-opposition to Delta Utilities’ request for approval of a blanket financing authorization for the issuance of long-term secured and unsecured debt, subject to the conditions within. This matter was considered at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                  ORDER NUMBER S-37932

     DELTA NORTH LOUISIANA GAS COMPANY, LLC, DELTA SOUTH LOUISIANA
         GAS COMPANY, LLC AND DELTA CAPITAL GAS COMPANY, LLC.

Docket No. S-37932, In re: Application for blanket financing authorization.

              (Decided at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                             ORDER

I.      INTRODUCTION

        The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“Commission”) considered Staff’s Report and

Recommendation, filed July 23, 2026, as amended, in the above-referenced proceeding (“Staff’s

Recommendation”) regarding the application of Delta North Louisiana Gas Company, LLC, Delta

South Louisiana Gas Company, LLC, and Delta Capital Gas Company, LLC (“Delta Utilities” or

the “Companies”) in this matter. Staff recommended the approval, with certain limited

modifications described in the body of this Order, of Delta Utilities’ request for approval of a

blanket financing authorization for the issuance of long-term secured and unsecured debt (the

“Application”). For the reasons set forth below, the Commission finds and determines that Staff’s

Recommendation, as amended, is reasonable considering the record, consistent with the law, and

not contrary to the public interest and is, therefore, approved. Delta Utilities’ blanket financing

authority is approved for the amounts and time periods described in this Order and is subject to the

reporting requirements contained in the ordering paragraphs of this Order.

II.     BACKGROUND AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY

        On May 19, 2026, Delta Utilities requested Commission approval of a blanket financing

authorization, to be effective from the date of the LPSC order in this proceeding through December

31, 2030, for the Companies to incur incremental long-term debt (debt with a term of more than

one year), up to a ceiling not to exceed certain per-company limits: Delta North – up to $200

million; Delta South – up to $195 million; and Delta Capital – up to $70 million (collectively, the

“Authorization Ceilings”).

        The Application requested the Commission to authorize expedited review and approval by

LPSC Staff of Delta Utilities’ individual financings, as applicable, without the need for additional

formal applications, docketing, Bulletin notices, ALJ proceedings, or votes of the Commission for

each individual financing within the scope of the Authorization Ceilings. The requested blanket


                                                                               Order No. S-37932
                                                                                          Page 1
 financing authorization would require the Companies to provide Staff with a 30-day advance

review for proposed financings, unless circumstances dictated a shorter period for review. In each

advance review, Delta Utilities would provide Staff detailed information about the respective

issuance, and if Staff determined the proposed issuance was acceptable, Staff would be authorized

to issue a letter of non-opposition for the proposed financing.

       The Application further requested that any periodic refinancing of debt prior to maturity

and any renewal, amendment, or replacement of the Companies’ existing revolving credit

agreements (or similar liquidity loan facility) would also be reviewed and authorized under the

blanket financing Staff review process but that the same would not count toward the Authorization

Ceilings. Advanced review and authorization by LPSC Staff under the blanket financing

procedures would not be required for short-term issuances (with a term of one year or less), and

extraordinary and special debt offerings, such as storm damage financings, would be excluded

from the blanket authorization process and, thus, would require separate applications for

Commission authorization.

       Notice of the Application was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin No. 1376,

dated May 22, 2026, with an intervention period of fifteen (15) days. No interventions were filed.

       Staff’s Recommendation was filed in this proceeding on July 23, 2026, recommending the

Commission grant Delta Utilities’ request for blanket financing authorization through the end of

2030. On August 14, 2026, Delta Utilities filed a letter expressing its non-opposition to Staff’s

Recommendation, subject to certain revisions and clarifications, as follows:

       Second sentence of Recommendation #2 being amended as follows:

       “In addition, any renewal, amendment, or replacement of Delta’s revolving credit
       agreements (or loan facility of similar liquidity), will also be reviewed and
       authorized under the blanket financing Staff review process, but that same would
       not count toward the $465 million total debt issuance ceiling amount.”

       Recommendation #5(d) being amended as follows:

       5.d. Any Delta presentations to credit rating agencies Delta’s projected leverage
       ratios for the next three (3) years in Excel format.

       Recommendation #5(f) being amended as follows:

       5.f. A recent run of the Delta corporate financial model extending three (3) years A
       current and projected capital structure for Delta over the next three (3) years.

       On August 31, 2026, Staff filed a letter in this proceeding accepting and agreeing with the

above revisions and clarifications to Staff’s Recommendation (“Staff’s Recommendation, as

amended”).

                                                                               Order No. S-37932
                                                                                          Page 2
 III.   COMMISSION JURISDICTION AND AUTHORITY

       The Commission exercises jurisdiction over all utility companies, including Delta Utilities,

pursuant Article IV, Section 21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974 and applicable Commission

Orders adopted pursuant to that authority. Article IV, Section 21 provides, in pertinent part:

               The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
               utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
               It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
               procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
               other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.

       Approval of the Application is required pursuant to the Commission’s General Order dated

November 13, 1996 (the “1996 Order”). In particular, the General Order states at Item Number 1:

               No public utility shall issue any security or assume any obligation
               or liability as guarantor, endorser, surety, or otherwise in respect of
               any security of any other public utility, or of any other person, until
               it has been authorized to do so by Order of this Commission.

Item Number 5 of the 1996 Order also provides:

               This General Order does not modify in any manner the General
               Order issued by this Commission dated March 18, 1994 related to
               Commission approval of sales, leases, etc. Any security issuance
               that requires a utility to “sell, assign, lease, transfer, mortgage, or
               otherwise dispose of or encumber” the property or assets of the
               utility must be approved by the Commission under standards set
               forth in the March 18, 1994 General Order as well.

       Further, approval of the Application is required pursuant to the Commission’s General

Order dated March 18, 1994 (the “1994 Order”) as the anticipated loan terms may require a pledge

of assets of the Companies to secure the funds.

IV.    STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION

       Based on Staff’s review of Delta Utilities’ Application and responses to Staff’s formal data

requests, including responses to the 18 points, pursuant to the 1994 Order, Staff believes that

approval of the blanket financing authorization is in the best interest of the public, as Delta

Utilities’ customers would reap the benefits of both Commission oversight and the most timely

and favorable debt financings available. Staff recommended the Commission express its non-

opposition to Delta Utilities’ request for blanket financing to incur incremental long-term debt

(with a term of more than one year), up to a ceiling not to exceed the per-company Authorization

Ceilings: Delta North – up to $200 million; Delta South – up to $195 million; and Delta Capital –

up to $70 million, through December 31, 2030, subject to certain conditions and reporting

procedures. These procedures ensure both regulatory oversight and customer protection. The

reporting requirements are designed to ensure that Staff is presented with sufficiently detailed

                                                                                 Order No. S-37932
                                                                                            Page 3
 information about a proposed issue during the advance review period and again after a financing

has closed, to provide meaningful and effective regulatory oversight. Staff’s Recommendation, as

amended, includes annual reporting obligations that are designed to allow for a detailed review by

Commission Staff of Delta Utilities’ credit ratings, financial outlook, and activities under its

blanket authority.

V.      COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

        This matter was considered at the Commission’s September 16, 2026 Business and

Executive Session. After discussing, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice

Chairman Coussan, with Commissioner Francis, and Commissioner Lewis concurring, and

Commissioner Campbell temporarily absent, the Commission voted to accept Staff’s

Recommendation, as amended.



THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED:

        The Staff’s Recommendation, as amended, is hereby accepted by this Commission and

that:

     1. Delta Utilities’ blanket financing authority, up to a ceiling not to exceed certain per-
        company limits—Delta North, up to $200 million; Delta South, up to $195 million;
        and Delta Capital, up to $70 million—through December 31, 2030, is prudent,
        reasonable, and in the best interest of Delta Utilities’ retail customers.

     2. Delta Utilities shall file notice into this docket in order to provide the LPSC Staff with
        a prior review opportunity of at least thirty (30) days in advance of any anticipated
        long-term debt issuance, or if that much advance review opportunity is not reasonably
        feasible due to the exigencies of the financing, such lesser amount of advance review
        opportunity as is reasonably possible under the circumstances. This advance review is
        not required for either draws on revolving credit agreements (described in paragraph 2,
        below) or for issuances of short-term debt (with a term of one year or less). If Staff has
        no objection to the specific long-term financing, and Staff hereby being authorized to
        do so, Staff shall issue a letter of non-opposition to Delta Utilities prior to the stated
        anticipated closing date for the specific financing. In such advance review opportunity
        given by Delta Utilities to Staff, Delta Utilities shall provide the following information
        pertaining to each proposed debt issue:

            a. Dollar amount of the issue;
            b. Timing of issue (i.e., anticipated schedule for issuance);
            c. Type of security and principal features (e.g., taxable or tax exempt, call
               protection, hedging characteristics, secured or unsecured);
            d. Rationale for the proposed structure;
            e. Term of the security;
            f. Method of issuance (e.g., public issuance, private placement, bank loan);
            g. Identity of the underwriters and other vendors handling the issuance and method
               of selection;
            h. Expected interest rate, including credit spreads, and indicative pricing; and
            i. Other estimated issuance expenses, including discounts or premiums.




                                                                                 Order No. S-37932
                                                                                            Page 4
    This informational list is not intended to restrict Staff from requesting additional
   pertinent information on an informal basis, and Delta Utilities shall reasonably
   cooperate with such requests.

3. Delta Utilities’ periodic refinancing of debt, prior to the debt’s maturity, in order to
   lower interest expense, also will be reviewed under the blanket financing arrangement,
   but will not count toward the $465 million total debt issuance ceiling amount, provided
   that Staff’s letter of non-opposition, issued pursuant to ordering paragraph 1 of this
   Order, so confirms. In addition, any renewal, amendment, or replacement of Delta
   Utilities’ revolving credit agreements (or loan facility of similar liquidity), will also be
   reviewed and authorized under the blanket financing Staff review process, but that
   same would not count toward the $465 million total debt issuance ceiling amount.

4. Expedited treatment under this blanket financing authorization will not be available for
   extraordinary and special debt offerings, such as storm damage securitization
   financings. For these extraordinary and special debt offerings, Delta Utilities would
   still need to file a request as a standalone docket.

5. Promptly following the closing of each unopposed long-term debt issuance, Delta
   Utilities shall provide LPSC Staff and file into the record of this docket the following
   information:
       a. Date of issuance;
       b. Date of maturity;
       c. Amount outstanding;
       d. Net proceeds;
       e. Interest rate;
       f. Debt discount or premiums and annual amortization;
       g. Issuance expenses (itemized, including hedging costs) and annual amortizations;
       h. Effective cost rate(s) for ratemaking purposes;
       i. Any difficulties encountered in issuance; and
       j. A description of any material differences in information previously provided to
           Staff pertaining to the issuance structure, cost, features or method of issuance, and
           reason for changes.

   This informational list is not intended to restrict Staff from requesting additional pertinent
   information on an informal basis, and Delta Utilities shall reasonably cooperate with such
   requests.

6. On an annual basis (by April 30 of each year, beginning April 30, 2027), and covering
   the period January 1 to December 31 of the immediately preceding calendar year) Delta
   Utilities shall file into the record an update for the Commission and its Staff a report on
   Delta Utilities’ activities under the blanket financing authorization. The annual filing
   shall include the following elements:

       a. All credit rating reports issued within the preceding year;
       b. The latest Delta Utilities annual financing statements (including, but not limited
          to, Delta Utilities’ balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements)
          for the preceding year;
       c. A description of any major changes in financial policies of Delta Utilities (e.g.,
          dividend policy, capital structure targets, etc.) that became effective within the
          preceding year;
       d. Delta Utilities’ projected leverage ratios for the next three (3) years in Excel
          format;
       e. A current statement of long-term debt outstanding and a schedule showing the
          embedded cost of debt calculations;
       f. A current and projected capital structure for Delta Utilities over the next three
          (3) years; and
       g. A schedule showing monthly amounts of Delta Utilities’ short-term debt and
          cost rate for the most recent twelve (12) months.

7. Notwithstanding the Commission’s approval of Delta Utilities’ blanket financing
   authorization, Staff reserves the right to oppose any specific long-term debt issuance.

                                                                              Order No. S-37932
                                                                                         Page 5
        Upon receipt of advance notice, Staff shall exercise best efforts and all due diligence to
       express any grounds of opposition to Delta Utilities at the earliest possible time. Delta
       Utilities and Staff shall cooperate to allow Staff a reasonable opportunity to express
       any objection to Delta Utilities prior to Delta Utilities’ stated anticipated closing date
       for the specific financing in order to facilitate the resolution of such objection prior to
       the stated anticipated closing date.

   8. Proceeds from the debt issuances pursuant to this Order shall be used only for Delta
      Utilities’ utility purposes and for the benefit of Delta Utilities’ retail customers. Such
      proceeds may not be used for the financing of any unregulated non-public utility
      operations of Delta Utilities, Delta Utilities’ parent(s), any entity possessing a
      controlling interest in Delta Utilities’ corporate parent, or any affiliate of Delta Utilities,
      and may not be used for the financing of any operations of any merchant utility affiliate
      of Delta Utilities, without in either case prior Commission authorization. Such debt
      issues pursuant to this Order: (a) must be for lawful object within the corporate
      purposes of Delta Utilities; (b) must be necessary and appropriate for and consistent
      with the performance by Delta Utilities of its service to the public; and (c) must not
      impair Delta Utilities’ ability to perform that service.

   9. This Order does not authorize Delta Utilities to change its retail rates, nor does it
      authorize or approve cost recovery for any debt issuance that takes place under the
      blanket authorization. Staff and any stakeholder retain their rights to take any position
      on the recovery of costs associated with the debt issuances that are covered by this
      blanket debt issuance authority in any future proceeding.

This Order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
October 12, 2026
